title: introduce mux credential proxy and async-zipstream ergonomics; cross-SDK auth/retry parity + minor bumps
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: multiple customers and internal teams asked for a small, well-tested primitive to let SDK users supply multiple credential sources (short-lived tokens from vaults, rotating delegated creds, and long-lived API keys) without wiring custom orchestration in app code. Separately, TS/Python/Go SDK consumers requested a simpler async composition primitive for chunked streaming responses (concatenate+throttle semantics) that preserves backpressure and parity across languages. This PR implements a lightweight "mux credential proxy" plus an ergonomic asyncZipStream helper in all three SDKs, reconciles retry window defaults across languages, and bumps SDK minors so applications can opt into the new primitives.

Changes in this PR (single-string description): - Add mux credential proxy: a small in-SDK coordinator that accepts an ordered list of CredentialProviders and exposes a single provider surface with deterministic rotation and lease metadata. It supports optional warmup hooks and pluggable clock (test-friendly). - Add asyncZipStream helper: accepts multiple chunked-async iterables (or Node streams) and yields zipped/interleaved chunks with configurable windowing and per-source backpressure policy. Replaces previous ad-hoc helper in examples and standardizes grammar across SDKs. - Normalize retry config: default connect/idle retire windows aligned to 2s connect / 60s idle across SDKs, introduce RetryProfile v2 that is opt-in. Documented migration notes. - Minor public API tidy: small ergonomics changes to StreamHandle.close() -> .stop(), clearer error subclassing for AuthError vs RetryExhausted, and documented stable deprecation of old helpers in favor of asyncZipStream. - Bump versions: ts 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0, python 0.18.4 -> 0.19.0, go v0.16.7 -> v0.17.0 (all semver-minor). Motivation: improve cross-language parity and reduce customer glue code for credential rotation and stream merging. Backwards compatibility: default runtime behavior preserved; rotation semantics only change when consumers pass multiple providers or opt into RetryProfile v2; the StreamHandle API rename includes a compatibility shim for one release.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc & compatibility review (ENG-2147) - [x] Tests added: unit + integration + interop smoke tests across local CI matrix - [x] Benchmarks: microbench for stream interleave latency and credential swap overhead - [x] Docs updated: SDK changelogs + migration snippet - [x] Version bumps and changelogs prepared - [x] Confirmed no behavioral change for single-provider consumers

Testing notes: Ran matrix in CI (linux/py38/py310, node14/node18, go1.21) + simulated vault lease rotation tests in python/ts. Benchmarks show mux proxy adds ~0.6ms median per-token for token-swap scenarios and asyncZipStream reduces end-to-end throughput variance in multi-source streams by ~18% at small window sizes. Migration: users should replace old example helper with asyncZipStream or keep the old helper for one cycle (compat shim present). If you supply multiple providers, consult README: merging semantics are FIFO by provider order.

review_comments: Diego Morales: +1 overall, left two nit comments about naming (stop vs close) and a comment about exposing lease metadata as part of Token object.
Lily Chen: requested clearer retry docs and an explicit migration section for users who depended on old shuffle semantics. Also asked for a perf test to measure rotation under load.
Samir Gupta: found a concurrency race in the Go mux when a provider returned error during swap; asked for a retry-with-backoff inside the rotation path. Patch pushed to address and tests added.
Asha Patel (author): replied to all comments, added compatibility shim for StreamHandle.close -> .stop(), clarified lease metadata surface, and added the requested perf test to the CI matrix.
release_notes: Introduce mux credential proxy (allows multiple credential providers with deterministic rotation and lease metadata); asyncZipStream helper for ergonomic multi-source chunked streaming; normalized retry defaults and opt-in RetryProfile v2; minor SDK bumps (ts 1.10.0, python 0.19.0, go v0.17.0). See docs/sdk-migration/mux-proxy-and-zipstream.md for migration guidance.
